overall.summary: The canonical project harness is profile-bound. A newly projected run containing valid PNG, MP4, WAV, MP3, and SRT assets mounted in Codex's in-app Browser with zero console warnings/errors. The MP4, WAV, and MP3 each reached readyState=4 with a two-second decoded duration; both native audio players advanced beyond 1.5 seconds without an error. A provider-free committed regression also generates valid media through the shared FFmpeg resolver and probes and fully decodes the content-addressed projected MP4, WAV, and MP3 copies. Host-cache parity, an accepted npm roster-signal exception, and real cross-platform UI smoke coverage remain open.

skillAndProfileEvidence.runtimeBinding: The formal video-harness production profile binds declared canonical paths and hashes and rejects development-only or undeclared global fallbacks.

findings.finding: Seven BuzzAssist skill IDs resolve to a current project canonical version and at least one divergent installed plugin-cache or external copy.
findings.impact: The formal harness remains deterministic because it binds the project path and hash, but ad-hoc skill discovery outside that harness cannot yet guarantee identical Claude Code and Codex content on this host.
findings.recommendation: Publish and install one reviewed stable bundle on both hosts, then require the inventory collision gate to report zero production-relevant divergent hashes before claiming host-wide parity.

findings.finding: The package audit passes only with two accepted channel-roster exceptions. Two packaged implementation files each contain four of eleven roster identifiers.
findings.impact: No Channel Pack directory, display name, or unresolved private path was packaged, but the npm boundary is not strictly free of channel-derived identifiers.
findings.recommendation: Replace the roster-specific identifiers with generic fixtures or keep those implementations outside the public tarball, then remove the exceptions and require status=clean.

findings.finding: The repository defines Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows CI and isolated setup simulations, but its test runner explicitly notes that a real UI mount test is not implemented.
findings.impact: Build and filesystem portability are covered by design; equal Canvas rendering, media controls, and host integration on real Windows/Linux and Claude Code are not empirically proven.
findings.recommendation: Add a small no-network fixture and browser mount smoke on every OS, plus separate Claude Code and Codex host acceptance runs, without adding a second Playwright dependency where the host Browser API is available.

findings.finding: Canvas media projection validates path containment, symlinks, SHA-256, extension, and declared MIME. The Browser smoke proves projected MP4 playback, and the committed provider-free regression uses the shared cross-platform FFmpeg resolver to generate valid H.264/AAC MP4, PCM WAV, and MP3 assets, projects them, verifies their content-addressed locations with ffprobe, and fully decodes every stream.
findings.impact: The projected media copies are now reproducibly proven decodable independently of a provider or browser. Cross-host UI parity remains a separate finding.
findings.recommendation: Keep the regression in the focused and release test suites.

findings.finding: Audio and BGM waveform cards now expose an explicit play control that opens one native audio player overlay. It accepts only normalized Canvas asset URLs, obtains tunnel access at runtime without persistence, and does not create a decoder for every visible card.
findings.impact: The production build and provider-free byte regression pass. In Codex's in-app Browser, both WAV narration and MP3 BGM opened the native player, reached readyState=4, reported a two-second duration, advanced playback beyond 1.5 seconds, and produced no console warning or error.
findings.recommendation: Repeat the same fixture on Claude Code and other operating systems under the cross-platform finding.

findings.finding: A minimal isolated run with a valid PNG, MP4, WAV, MP3, and SRT was projected through the new harness-run media namespace and mounted in Codex's in-app Browser.
findings.impact: The current host has end-to-end visual proof for the new projection path, including MP4 playback metadata and zero console warnings/errors.
findings.recommendation: Repeat the same fixture as a release acceptance run on Claude Code, Windows, and Linux before claiming cross-host parity.

findings.finding: Canonical harness skills live under .agents/skills and are promoted into the staged plugin skills directory by the official setup script. The raw npm package plugin manifest points at the generic skills directory.
findings.impact: The supported setup and updater route can share the canonical skills, but treating the raw tarball as a directly installable complete harness would omit that promotion step.
findings.recommendation: Keep official setup as the only supported install path, or make the published artifact staging step explicit and test raw-artifact installation.

findings.finding: At least one legacy video element in the current local Canvas retains an absolute source path in custom data. The new projection intentionally omits source absolute paths.
findings.impact: This is local-state privacy and portability debt, not an npm tarball leak.
findings.recommendation: Provide a one-time local Canvas migration that removes legacy source paths after content-addressed assets are confirmed.

findings.finding: When disk exhaustion caused save HTTP 500 responses, failures were visible in the console but no durable operator-facing recovery proof was observed.
findings.impact: An operator could continue editing while persistence is failing.
findings.recommendation: Surface a persistent save-failed state with retry guidance and an explicit recovered/saved acknowledgement.
